snip.t: This is infantile pyloric stenosis, with a hypochloraemic, hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis (not acidosis).
snip.s: Paediatrics end of fourth year main exam: 1 July 2019, Paper One, 99 of 100 MCQs

snip.t: ❖ Diagnosis: Classically, pyloric stenosis has been confirmed by performing a test feed,\nwhere the baby is given a milk feed which initially calms the hungry infant, and allows for\nexamination.
Gastric outlet obstruction: chronic ulcer scarring leads to pyloric stenosis; presents with vomiting of undigested food.

Pyloric stenosis Recurrent ​projectile nonbilious​ vomiting Ultrasonography​ of pylorus\nimmediately after feeding in neonates\naged 2-12 wk​, infrequent stools Upper Gl contrast study if ultrasonography
(pyloric stenosis) - watery diarrhea(can indicate a VIP secreting neuroblastoma)

When symptoms of vomiting predominate, one should consider other diseases such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), diabetic ketoacidosis, pyloric stenosis, acute abdomen, or urinary tract infection.
